title: The Rules We’re Using to Design Our Lives in 2026
summary: Cherie and Jean walk through the goal-setting and reflection systems they personally use each January: a word of the year, Cherie's 5x5 bingo card, Jean's '37 things while I'm 37' list with a theme and daily scripting, and vision boards. They then model three end-of-2025 reflection questions and three projected end-of-2026 questions, concluding that 2025 was a grind/building year and that 2026 needs rest, play, saying no, outside help, and less caring what others think.

ideas.idea: The biggest mistake people make in January is rushing into the new year without reflecting on the previous one.
ideas.detail: The hosts cite Harvard researchers finding that a few minutes reflecting on your performance improves the next round of performance by 18%.

ideas.idea: The stretch between January 1 and the Lunar New Year is a natural 'neutral zone' for slow, intentional planning, so there is no rush to finish goals by January 1.
ideas.detail: They apply William Bridges' Transitions framework (the neutral zone comes after an ending and before a new beginning) and note Lunar New Year (Year of the Fire Horse) falls on February 17, giving a six-week transition window.

ideas.idea: Fresh starts at temporal milestones like a new year or birthday genuinely work as reset points.
ideas.detail: The hosts reference the Wharton 'Fresh Start Effect' study showing landmarks are good times to reset and start anew.

ideas.idea: Pick one word or phrase of the year as the simplest focusing framework, since a long list of goals can be overwhelming.
ideas.detail: Cherie's 2026 word is 'play' (her 2025 word in hindsight was 'grind'); Jean chose a series: fun, ease, joy, light, abundance and breakout. This takes 30 seconds to 3 minutes.

ideas.idea: A 5x5 bingo card of activities turns vague visions into tactical, activity-based goals that describe a full, balanced year.
ideas.detail: Cherie's 2025 card mixed work and personal items: fall in love, make kimchi, host a dinner party, ski a new mountain, read 12 books, volunteer three times, gym 30 days in a row, speak at a conference; a vision like 'make the podcast a success' becomes a metric like hitting 100K YouTube subscribers.

ideas.idea: Reviewing last year's goals reveals patterns; Cherie's all go-go-go 2025 card taught her that 2026 must include rest and recovery.
ideas.detail: The 'gym 30 days in a row' goal was not healthy and she hurt her back, so her 2026 card will include five massages and a Korean spa scrub; she writes the card in Sharpie and is taking weeks to finalize it deliberately.

ideas.idea: Jean's '37 things while I'm 37' system: write a theme paragraph, a scripted average day, and categorized goals across health, relationships, career, family, growth, mindset, creativity, finances, personal care and fun.
ideas.detail: Her 2025 theme was 'making big moves and believing everything will work out in my favor,' tapping the energy she had entering HBS ten years earlier; she tracked gym visits in 156 boxes and lists something to look forward to for each month.

ideas.idea: List far more goals than you need (69 to hit 37) so you can include trivial, guaranteed and wildly aspirational items and still finish the year feeling 100% successful.
ideas.detail: Jean used to feel dissatisfied hitting 20 of 36, so she expanded the list; items ranged from 'file taxes on time' and 'donate clothes' to attending her Dartmouth 15-year reunion.

ideas.idea: Vision boards work by keeping your vision in front of you daily so you subconsciously work toward it, and they only have to make sense to you.
ideas.detail: The sisters have vision-boarded for ten years, made their biggest posters ever for 2026 from magazine clippings (jewelry, travel, fruit, horses for the Fire Horse year), and Cherie has hosted vision board parties for girlfriends at Stanford.

ideas.idea: Use both written and visual planning tools because they engage different sides of the brain; start small and build the system up over years.
ideas.detail: Jean pairs her multi-page written plan with an all-visual board; they stress you can do 10% of what they do, e.g. write down 10 or 15 things, and evolve it annually.

ideas.idea: Use three end-of-year reflection questions: one word for the year, your biggest failure, and one thing to leave behind.
ideas.detail: Cherie's 2025 word was 'grind,' Jean's was 'building' (and rebuilding herself after nearly a decade partnered, now single, an entrepreneur and in media); a longer question list is in the episode description.

ideas.idea: Sweat equity builds the foundation, but a grind year needs to be followed by one that is more efficient and more fun to be sustainable.
ideas.detail: Both sisters were near burnout by the end of 2025 from building Tiger Sisters; Jean's biggest failure was losing balance after the show took off in summer, culminating in crying at a celebratory dinner at Jon & Vinny's.

ideas.idea: Naming your biggest failure matters because it is the thing you can change going forward rather than repeat.
ideas.detail: Jean says she is proud of what they built and would not change how they did it, but she can change how she goes about 2026.

ideas.idea: Be more discerning about who gets your love and trust; don't give your all to friends who have not demonstrated they can be trusted or reciprocate.
ideas.detail: Cherie's biggest failure was falling into a repeated pattern of declaring someone a 'soul sister,' pouring in time and energy and introducing them to family, then finding it unreciprocated; she wants to protect her heart while remaining kind.

ideas.idea: Stop caring what acquaintances think of you; people who talk about people negatively are a different category from people who talk about ideas and growth.
ideas.detail: Jean wants to leave behind worrying about whether old friends mock her evolution; she cites a podcast clip where a creator suspected friends were sharing clips of him and the response was that they are not his friends.

ideas.idea: Answer forward-looking questions as if the year has already ended: what was your headline, what resources did you need, and what did you say no to.
ideas.detail: Both sisters' 2026 headline is 'breakout' and 'Tiger Sisters goes mainstream,' and they ask listeners to say it with them to manifest it.

ideas.idea: Consistent therapy and daily journaling are the resources for working out your emotions and getting thoughts out of your head.
ideas.detail: Cherie has done therapy consistently for over a year and plans to keep it and a morning journaling habit through 2026.

ideas.idea: To break out you have to stop being self-reliant and bring in help, both in business and in life.
ideas.detail: Jean says in 2025 they did not bring in enough outside resources; a stylist, Emily Tyra, is one recent addition and 2026 should include a long list of people supporting them.

ideas.idea: Your power lies in the ability to say no, including saying no to yourself and your instinct to do a zillion things.
ideas.detail: Cherie will say no to distractions from Tiger Sisters and to her own urge to travel every other weekend, and suggests a 'things I won't do this year' list as another exercise.
